title: Ginger Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Ginger Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Ginger nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus in luya, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Ginger nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your luya (ginger) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, magnesium, zinc, iron and calcium. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Nitrogen deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for ginger
heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc, iron and calcium stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which ginger nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Ginger nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the old leaves of luya

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a ginger nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest ginger nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in ginger

Older leaves turn pale or yellow, starting low and moving up. Reddish tints can creep from the leaf edges toward the midrib. Leaves stay small, plants are stunted and roots weak, and the rhizome yield drops. You see it most at this stage: from 2 to 5 months after planting, during tillering.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in luya
Sandy or worn out soils, heavy rain washing nitrogen away, and little or no fertilizer. Ginger takes up large amounts of nutrients.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur deficiency yellows veins and all on the young leaves too. Bacterial wilt yellows leaves quickly with rotting, foul smelling rhizomes. To be sure, check that the old leaves yellowed first. Soil test.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Give a general need of 180 kg N, 180 kg P2O5 and 255 kg K2O per hectare. Split the nitrogen through the season. For quick help give a 1 percent urea spray (10 g per liter, 160 g in a 16 liter sprayer). Repeat it every 15 days.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea (46 0 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Ammonium Chloride** by La Filipina (25 0 0), **Agripower 46 0 0 (Locally Blended) Coated** by Green Acres Agri Tech and **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, mix decomposed organic matter into the furrows before planting, and mulch with rice straw or coconut leaves. Let a soil test and the crop's color set the season's nitrogen.
Potassium deficiency in ginger

The edges of older leaves turn yellow, then burn or scorch, and dead spots form in the leaf. Internodes stay short, plants wilt easily and growth is stunted. You see it most at this stage: rhizome bulking.
Why potassium deficiency happens in luya
Sandy and acid soils, and fields not given potash. Ginger needs more potash than nitrogen.
How to tell it apart
Leaf spot disease gives spots with a yellow ring scattered over the leaf, not edge burn. To be sure, soil test for potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Give a general need of 180 kg N, 180 kg P2O5 and 255 kg K2O per hectare. Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 in splits. Give a 1 percent potassium chloride spray (10 g per liter, 160 g in a 16 liter sprayer).

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash (MOP)** by Atlas Fertilizer (0 0 60), **Simplot Sulfate 0 0 50** by Nutranta, **Potassium Nitrate** by Parafield (13 0 46) and **Qrop Mix Production 14 0 23 plus 13 Cao** by Farmtech Agriland (14 0 23 with 9.3 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep the soil pH above 6 and add wood ash or compost. Test the soil every two or three years.
Phosphorus deficiency in ginger

Plants look darker green than healthy ones, with purple color on the leaf undersides. Older leaves yellow from the tip to the base, roots are poor and rhizomes small and stunted. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in luya
Acid and volcanic soils that hold phosphorus.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency gives pale plants, not dark. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Give a general need of 180 kg N, 180 kg P2O5 and 255 kg K2O per hectare. Use single superphosphate for a quick fix and rock phosphate for the long term, following the soil test. Put it in at planting: phosphorus given late helps little.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Philphos 18 46 0 (Di Ammonium Phosphate)**, **Atlas Super Gro (16 20 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Granular Single Super Phosphate** by La Filipina (0 18 0 with 11 percent sulfur) and **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals (0 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, mix phosphorus and compost into the furrows at planting.
Magnesium deficiency in ginger

Leaves yellow between the veins while the veins stay green, and brown dead spots spread from the tips or edges. Leaves curl or cup, and old leaves can show a triangular arrowhead pattern near the stalk. Rhizomes stay small. You see it most at this stage: mid season.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in luya
Acid, sandy soils and heavy potash.
How to tell it apart
Potassium deficiency burns the edges without the green vein pattern. To be sure, soil test for magnesium.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

Give about 80 kg magnesium sulfate per hectare in bands near the plants. Apply it apart from potash. Use Dolomite on acid soils over the long run. Put the soil dose in before planting or when the rains begin. Sprays show results in 10 to 14 days.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium), **DDDD Planter's Choice Magnesium Sulphate Monohydrate** by Modern Time (15.1 percent magnesium) and **Zetryl MAG 9** by Zetryl Chem (9 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils with dolomite. Test the soil every two or three years.
Zinc deficiency in ginger
Leaves yellow between the veins and come out small, distorted and puckered, bunched in a rosette at the top. Plants branch less and roots are short. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why zinc deficiency happens in luya
High pH soils and heavy phosphorus.
How to tell it apart
Iron deficiency bleaches the young leaves without the bunching. To be sure, soil test for zinc. In a soil test, less than 0.8 ppm of zinc is low.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Give about 20 kg Zinc sulfate per hectare to the soil, or in severe cases a morning spray of 2 g zinc sulfate with 2.5 g lime per liter. Keep zinc and phosphate applications apart. Give the soil dose at planting or when the rains begin, and sprays on young growth.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester (22 percent zinc), **Petbowe Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** (33 percent zinc), **Tierramino ZN** by Unilox Far East Resources (7 0 0 with 10 percent zinc) and **Liquid Chelate Zinc with Sulfur** by Sagrex (10 percent zinc and 5 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep the soil pH between 5 and 7.5. Test the soil every two or three years.
Iron deficiency in ginger
Young leaves yellow between the veins while the veins stay green, then turn pale white. Rhizomes stay small. You see it most at this stage: early to mid growth.
Why iron deficiency happens in luya
High pH or limey soils, waterlogging, and low potassium.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur deficiency looks similar but yellows veins too. To be sure, soil test, since many soils have plenty of iron. The cause is often pH or waterlogging. In a soil test, less than 4.5 ppm of iron is low.
What to apply for iron deficiency

Give a 0.5 percent ferrous sulfate spray (5 g per liter, 80 g in a 16 liter sprayer). Give about 15 kg ferrous sulfate per hectare to the soil. Spray the young leaves in the cool of the day, soon after sunrise or near sunset.

Sold here with iron: **DDDD Planter's Choice Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Modern Time (19 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl Chem (30 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulphate Monohydrate** by Newman Chemicals (30 percent iron) and **Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, plant on well drained raised beds. Test the soil every two or three years. Keep organic matter up with compost, manure or crop residues.
Calcium deficiency in ginger
Young leaves crinkle, twist or grow unevenly, and their edges die. Plants are small and weak, and roots are stunted, misshapen and decay. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why calcium deficiency happens in luya
Very acid soils and high phosphorus. Heavy potash or ammonium fertilizer, salty soil and dry spells keep calcium from reaching fruit and young leaves.
How to tell it apart
Boron deficiency also deforms young leaves, with white rolled tips. To be sure, soil pH and calcium test. A soil test for calcium and pH, and a leaf test, confirm it.
What to apply for calcium deficiency
On acid soils, lime about 250 kg per hectare where the pH is 5.5 to 6. About 840 kg per hectare in two splits where it is 3.5 to 4.5. On alkaline soils use Gypsum.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** (36.2 percent calcium), **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium) and **Philphos Gypsum** (22.2 percent calcium and 17.4 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid uplands ahead of planting. Test the soil every two or three years. Keep potash in balance with magnesium and calcium.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any ginger nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your luya needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Ginger nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my luya leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: lower leaves turn pale yellow, leaves are small and the clump grows weak. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in ginger?
items.a: Give a general need of 180 kg N, 180 kg P2O5 and 255 kg K2O per hectare. Split the nitrogen through the season.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in ginger?
items.a: Give a general need of 180 kg N, 180 kg P2O5 and 255 kg K2O per hectare. Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 in splits.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in ginger?
items.a: Give a general need of 180 kg N, 180 kg P2O5 and 255 kg K2O per hectare. Use single superphosphate for a quick fix and rock phosphate for the long term, following the soil test.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my luya lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the ginger nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
